subject: P1 — LumenPay: throughput collapse after KV-cache pruning
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@lumenpay.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: LumenPay SRE <sre@lumenpay.com>
Date: 2028-03-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: P1 — LumenPay: sustained p99 spike + 500s after KV pruning

Folks,

We're seeing a sharp production regression starting ~08:45 UTC after the change your team applied to KV cache pruning on our dedicated pool. Symptoms: p99 latency jumped from ~120ms to 2.1s, throughput dropped by ~45%, and we started seeing 500s on inference tail requests. This is customer-facing — multiple merchants reported checkout slowdowns.

Attached is a triage bundle (lumenpay-incident-logs.zip) including request traces and our Grafana snapshots (slo-dashboard-snap.png). Our SRE thinks the failure mode looks like HOL blocking where small TTL/prefix pruning is evicting hot keys and causing request serialization.

We need an immediate rollback or guidance on a fast mitigation. Can your on-call join a quick screen-share? We can be available now.

— Samira
Samira Khan
Head of Platform Reliability, LumenPay
samira@lumenpay.com

Samira — thanks for the quick flag. I'm on it and looping in Priyom and Marissa to triage immediately.

Immediate plan:
- We will revert the KV pruning change in the LumenPay pool to the previous pruning window (rollforward -> rollback) as a hotfix.
- Priyom to validate hot keys + KV eviction rate and check for prefix cache misrouting.
- Marissa will monitor canary traffic post-rollback and watch p99 / 5xx.
- We'll schedule a 30-min bridge — provisioning now.

Rough ETA for rollback: 20–30 minutes depending on warmup. I will update here as soon as it's started.

Apologies for the impact — we'll treat this as P1.

— Rishi

Quick triage notes (initial):
- After reproducing on a staging snapshot: aggressive KV pruning reduced retained prefix entries by ~62%. Hot prefixes are being evicted, which pushes requests to cold-path model loads. That aligns with the HOL-like queuing we see.
- We also noticed the batcher falling back to single-request batches for ~18% of requests because prefix hits are missing; this increases per-token compute and amplifies queueing.
- Config diff is attached (kv-config-diff.txt): you can see TTL lowered from 30m -> 30s and aggressive prefix shard eviction enabled.

Next actions I started:
- Rolling back TTL/pruning flags to previous values now (start 10:08 UTC).
- Enabling soft-prefetch for the top-200 prefixes to avoid cold loads during warmup.
- Increasing batch max-window to allow short coalescing backlog for 30s while we recover.

I'll post verification metrics in ~10–15 minutes.

— Priyom
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: P1 — LumenPay: sustained p99 spike + 500s after KV pruning

Samira — final update for the hotfix we applied: rollback completed at 14:12 PDT and we validated progressive warmup.

What we did:
- Reverted pruning TTL to 30m and disabled aggressive prefix shard eviction (roll back to config before 2028-03-19 08:30 UTC).
- Enabled soft-prefetch for top-200 prefixes while caches warmed.
- Relaxed batcher window temporarily (max-window +20ms) to allow more natural coalescing for the next 30 minutes.

Outcome:
- Observed p99 fall from 2.1s -> 140ms within 9 minutes of rollback; throughput recovered to ~96% baseline within 18 minutes. 5xxs dropped back to normal levels.

Next steps / action items:
- We'll run a targeted post-mortem (internal + joint with LumenPay) to review the change-control and automated safety gates; invite scheduled for tomorrow 11:00 PDT. Link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c4-lumenpay-postmortem
- Priyom to produce a short runbook for KV pruning windows and a canary checklist for cache-sensitive flags.
- Laura: we will draft a credit proposal and a summary for exec log.

Samira, if you'd like an immediate walk-through of the config diff and mitigation, we're available. Sorry again for the disruption — we'll own the follow-up and deliver a concrete set of safety constraints to avoid HOL/cold-path cascades going forward.

— Rishi
Director, Production Reliability
Redwood Inference
